title: BrandLockup.prompt
universal_lens: The BrandLockup primitive formalizes a topological projection of high-dimensional brand identity onto constrained spatial manifolds. It enforces strict horizontal non-stacking constraints, utilizing continuous gradient mappings and discrete compactification operators to maintain structural invariance across varying viewport geometries and ambient luminosity conditions.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the lockup acts as a conformal prior for visual data streams. The `compact` operator functions as a Bayesian dimensionality reduction, collapsing posterior distributions into minimal sufficient statistics (emblem + GSE) under tight bandwidth constraints, while preserving maximum likelihood signal-fade gradients for optimal human-machine interface calibration.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the lockup defines a state-transition system over UI layouts. The `kinetic` flag triggers a one-shot temporal impulse upon page load, subject to accessibility boundary conditions (`prefers-reduced-motion`). This ensures deterministic rendering trajectories that adapt dynamically to environmental context without violating invariant branding axioms.

primitives.name: Horizontal Gradient Projection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Renders the approved chrome emblem (Brand Bible v1.0) alongside the "GALAXY SPORTS EDGE" wordmark set in Exo 2 with the signal-fade gradient (cyan -> magenta -> violet) and the signal underline.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Gradient vector \vec{\nabla} \in \mathbb{R}^3 (dimensionless RGB/HSV space); Horizontal axis x \in [0, W] pixels.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a strictly linear color interpolation space and fixed typographic metrics for Exo 2 font family.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if viewport width W falls below the minimum legible threshold of the wordmark, forcing an illegal vertical stack.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to projecting a high-dimensional semantic brand vector onto a 1D spatial manifold while preserving chromatic variance.
layer2.telemetry: Chromatic contrast ratio against background; pixel-perfect alignment delta.

primitives.name: Compact Dimensionality Reduction
primitives.verbatim_quote: `compact` collapses to emblem + "GSE" for the tightest rails.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Spatial constraint C \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} (pixels); Collapsed state S_c = (Emblem, "GSE").
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the emblem and 'GSE' substring retain full informational entropy of the parent brand entity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the reduced glyph cluster exceeds the tight rail constraint C, causing overflow or clipping.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a kernel density estimation where the full wordmark is pruned to its highest-probability tokens under severe spatial pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Bounding box width of rendered component vs. allocated rail width.

primitives.name: Kinetic Temporal Impulse
primitives.verbatim_quote: `kinetic` plays a one-shot arrival sting on full page load (disabled under prefers-reduced-motion).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Time t \in \mathbb{R}; Accessibility flag A \in \{0, 1\}; Animation function f(t) with Dirac-like onset.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a synchronous DOM load event and a globally accessible media query listener for motion preferences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if the animation loop fails to terminate (one-shot violation) or if accessibility flags are ignored, causing infinite motion.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a transient excitation in a dynamical system, immediately damped to zero energy state unless overridden by user preference priors.
layer2.telemetry: Animation duration in milliseconds; boolean check of `prefers-reduced-motion`.

reasoning_traces.think:
The BrandLockup primitive is mathematically derived as a constrained optimization problem over a 2D rendering canvas. We define a state space \Omega representing all possible visual configurations of the Galaxy Sports Edge identity. The primary operator, Horizontal Gradient Projection, maps the abstract brand vector B \in \mathbb{R}^N to a 1D spatial layout L(x), enforcing a strict non-stacking constraint: \forall x_1, x_2 \in L, y(x_1) = y(x_2). This ensures topological consistency across varying resolutions. The chromatic mapping utilizes a continuous signal-fade gradient \vec{\nabla}(t) transitioning from cyan to magenta to violet, acting as a smooth interpolation function over the wordmark's bounding box. When spatial constraints tighten beyond a critical threshold \epsilon, the Compact Dimensionality Reduction operator activates. This acts as a lossy compression kernel, projecting the full wordmark onto a minimal sufficient statistic subspace spanned by the emblem and the 'GSE' acronym. This preserves the core eigenvalues of brand recognition while minimizing spatial footprint. Finally, the Kinetic Temporal Impulse introduces a time-dependent variable T(t). Upon system initialization (page load), a one-shot animation function A(t) is triggered, modeled as a decaying exponential or Dirac-like pulse. However, this transition is gated by an accessibility predicate P_{motion}. If P_{motion} is true (prefers-reduced-motion), the kinetic operator is nulled, ensuring the system remains in a static equilibrium. The dualities lie between the expansive full lockup and the compressed compact form, balanced by the rigid horizontal invariant. Failure modes emerge when the viewport width approaches zero, causing the compact glyphs to collide, or when the gradient interpolation suffers from precision loss in low-bit color environments.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to early 20th-century Bauhaus grid systems, which sought to reduce visual communication to essential geometric primitives. Mathematically, it inherits from projective geometry, specifically the preservation of collinearity under perspective transformations. In modern computational theory, it mirrors responsive design paradigms pioneered by Ethan Marcotte, translating fluid typography and flexible grids into strict algebraic constraints. The kinetic aspect borrows from Hamiltonian mechanics, treating UI transitions as energy-minimizing paths constrained by user accessibility potentials.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the decision actor—the frontend engineer or automated layout engine—as an agent optimizing for two competing utilities: brand fidelity and spatial efficiency. The agent observes the environment (viewport dimensions, theme mode) and selects an action (render full, render compact, enable/disable kinetic). Opposing agents include the user's cognitive load and accessibility requirements. If the user prefers reduced motion, the agent must veto the kinetic impulse to avoid sensory overload. The lockup acts as a shared mental model, ensuring that regardless of the agent's chosen configuration, the resulting visual output remains instantly recognizable as the authoritative Galaxy Sports Edge entity.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity vetoes are critical here. The horizontal layout must never collapse into a vertical stack; any attempt by the CSS flexbox algorithm to wrap lines must be intercepted and vetoed by the `nowrap` invariant. Leakage occurs if the signal-fade gradient bleeds outside the wordmark's bounding box, contaminating adjacent UI elements. Furthermore, the kinetic animation must be strictly bounded in time; an infinite loop would violate the one-shot assumption and leak computational resources. The `prefers-reduced-motion` check acts as a hard veto gate, overriding any default kinetic state to ensure compliance with accessibility standards, preventing a failure mode where dynamic content impedes user agency.
